resume_behavior: The interrupted run resumed by reloading the best saved checkpoint with a fresh AdamW optimizer: an interrupted continuation, not an exact optimizer-state resume.
model: Original neural path: pretrained DistilBERT with two-class head, embeddings and lower 4 transformer layers frozen under free local resource limits; top layers and head fine-tuned.

data.selection: Exact-text deduplicated, seeded Python RNG (20261125). Pool of 1500 per class shuffled, first 1500 combined kept (near-balanced, actual counts recorded: 587 toxic / 613 non-toxic fit). Development carve-out is exactly 150 per class; remainder fits. Only the data-selection RNG was seeded in the executed run; training order and dropout were not deterministically seeded, so retraining does not reproduce the exact weights.

checkpoint_selection.rule_intended: Best development F1 with the two-logit softmax scorer.
checkpoint_selection.rule_actually_applied: SUPERSEDED: epoch selection during the executed run scored development with sigmoid(logit1) instead of softmax over both logits. Under that wrong scorer epoch 1 (F1 .8012) beat epoch 2 (F1 .7762), so the epoch-1 checkpoint was saved. Only the epoch-1 checkpoint persists; epoch-2 weights were not retained, so re-selection under the correct scorer is impossible. The corrected metrics below evaluate the persisted epoch-1 checkpoint as-is and do NOT imply it is the best checkpoint under the correct scorer.
checkpoint_selection.threshold_note: Softmax prob >= 0.5 tests logit1 >= logit0 while the legacy sigmoid(logit1) >= 0.5 tests logit1 >= 0; the methods disagree whenever sign(logit1) != sign(logit1 - logit0). Verified empirically from the persisted Nx2 logits: 0 of 300 development rows meet that condition, so the two scorers necessarily produce identical predictions, confusion (TP137/FP55/FN13/TN95) and threshold metrics on this checkpoint and slice; only the ranking metrics (ROC-AUC, average precision) change. This is an observed property of this checkpoint on this slice, not a general equivalence. Per-row logits and both scorers' predictions are preserved for audit.

dev_metrics_threshold_0.5.scorer: softmax over both logits; ROC-AUC and average precision from sklearn 1.6.1 standard implementations

superseded_legacy_metrics.note: Original report values, kept for audit only. Scored with sigmoid(logit1) and custom rank-metric code whose ROC curve omitted the origin and whose average precision handled ties non-standardly. Do not cite.
superseded_legacy_metrics.rescore_reproduction_check: The post-hoc rescore reproduced every legacy threshold metric and both custom rank metrics exactly (TP137/FP55/FN13/TN95, AUC .87631, AP .84321) from the persisted checkpoint and the seeded selection, confirming the development slice and checkpoint are unchanged; only the scorer changed.

limits: Development slice carved from an already fully exposed source; not an untouched benchmark and not natural prevalence (development balanced by construction). Partial fine-tune under 2 GB free RAM, not full fine-tuning. Not comparable in rank to the TF-IDF baseline: selection, size and split differ. Probabilities are not calibrated risk. Labels are averaged annotator judgments, no subgroup fairness evaluation. Do not automate punitive moderation decisions from this model.
